reopened_from: old Makin stand-off raid / USS Franks named result

Japanese_light_group.why_same_hulls: No new causal path changes which four already-forward destroyers can reach the first 26/27-night window. CL/heavier units remain farther back or committed to cover/reinforcement roles.
Japanese_light_group.target_choice: Tarawa outer support/transport concentration replaces Makin as centered target because organized Tarawa resistance remains high-intensity and CVE/transport/bombardment shipping remains fixed there.
Japanese_light_group.mission: stand-off Type 93 attack on outer screen / support traffic; no inner-anchorage penetration and no prolonged gun battle

cue_chain.event: Degraded Marshall long-range reconnaissance/night-air reports plus radio bearings refresh the Tarawa support concentration broadly; no exact CVE anchorage map is obtained.

Japanese destroyers approach at high speed from the Marshall side while using passive emission awareness/optics; US outer SG screen is already alert after the daytime carrier battle and continuing Japanese reconnaissance.
US SG obtains the first reliable surface track at roughly 22-27 km class. US outer-screen destroyers turn to engage and the transport/support concentration begins emergency maneuver.
Japanese group launches its immediate first torpedo salvo from roughly 16-18 km and turns away before radar-directed gunfire can develop into a prolonged action.

torpedo_accounting.reason: Hatsuzuki/Suzutsuki contribute one quadruple mount each and Hamakaze/Fujinami one octuple battery each. The old 28-32 centered launch over-counted immediate tubes for an attack that turns away at once.
torpedo_accounting.second_salvo: NOT centered. Branch reload/second-effective-salvo capability exists, but the SG-contact stand-off doctrine requires immediate withdrawal; no 12-20 minute reload engagement is accepted here.

centered_result.US: One outer-screen destroyer takes one Type 93 hit and is lost/abandoned centered. Exact hull name remains OPEN until the Tarawa night-screen OOB is individually closed. No centered CVE/APA/LST hit; one additional transport-area hit remains a sensitivity branch only.
centered_result.Japan: Fujinami takes one light-to-moderate 5-inch/splinter damage event during radar-directed return fire, keeps withdrawal speed. Other three destroyers avoid mission-kill.
centered_result.air_followup: A small 5-7 aircraft Japanese night harassment/recon wave arrives during/after withdrawal, scores no centered ship hit, loses 1-2 aircraft, and increases US reluctance to conduct a long chase outside the transport screen.

Tarawa_ground_coupling: For roughly 60-100 minutes some US destroyer/outer-cover attention shifts seaward. This reduces immediate night naval-fire responsiveness but does not remove artillery, M4A2, machine-gun or all destroyer support. Japanese infiltration gains a local temporary benefit only.

heavy_surface_gate.reason: Tarawa persistence and the daytime Lexington hit increase attraction, but Kongo/CA heavy cover is not physically positioned for a 26/27-night strike without a daylight approach on 27 Nov under still-large US fast-carrier/CVE air power. No teleporting heavy-force rescue run.

named_result_guard: Old USS Franks DD-554 sinking is VOID as a named fact in this rerun until screen OOB closure; centered loss is currently one unnamed US outer-screen DD.
